goals.label: Camp authorities and militia control food distribution
Commander's authority and appearance of strength
Commander's leverage with government and FWB for funding and resources
Commander's personal safety and freedom from retaliation or prosecution
FWB keeps independent control and oversight of food distribution
FWB meets donor accountability and documentation requirements
FWB neutrality: aid does not feed or pay armed guards or militia
FWB staff and assistants are safe from threats or violence
FWB staff have sufficient access and movement inside the camp
FWB's reputation and visibility of its work
Food aid is diverted, skimmed or confiscated before reaching refugees
Food distributions trigger riots or violence in the camp
Food is distributed fairly without discrimination among refugee groups
Generators stay powered with fuel and parts for security
Guards and their families are fed and compensated, keeping guards loyal
Host community and local economy are protected and supportive
Refugees receive adequate, nutritionally sufficient food
Refugees stay contained in the camp and do not reach the capital
Refugees suffer abuse, violence or collective punishment by guards
Riots, unrest or violence break out in the camp
Steady, ongoing food supply reaches the camp
Unrest or visible abuse draws international attention, political or legal costs
Commander's relationship and trust with the Senior Militia Leader
FWB-selected independent or local staff work in the camp
Refugees' needs and views shape the assistance
Resource-heavy nutritional assessments are carried out and cause delays

redLines.label: Hire local workers or local partners such as MASHA for distribution
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Provide food rations to guards and their families, or food as payment for guards
redLines.quote: If they see the refugees eating better than they are, they may well rebel, and it may be your head. Or someone in your family's head.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
